automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.policy: Only public web sources with a visible publication or update date inside the last 2 days relative to the run time were included. Missing, ambiguous, future-dated, stale, boundary-only, and upstream-only candidates were excluded.

federation_boundary.downstream_scope: This wiki records AI-assisted development practice, operating model, verification, governance, workflow, and local adoption implications.
federation_boundary.upstream_scope: The upstream AI wiki owns broad ecosystem entity coverage for companies, models, products, developer tools, agentic frameworks, MCP servers, and broad techniques.
federation_boundary.application_in_this_run: Broad GitHub Copilot, GitHub, JetBrains, OpenAI Codex, Claude Code, MCP, model-family, and product availability facts were either marked upstream-owned in qualifying items or excluded when no local practice implication was identified.

qualifying_updates.title: Copilot code review adds API requests and Balanced default
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: GitHub announced that Copilot code review can now be requested through REST and GraphQL APIs, with a per-request review effort level. Balanced became the default review effort for new and existing repositories and organizations unless Lite was explicitly selected.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: AI code review is becoming a scriptable lifecycle step rather than only a pull-request sidebar action. Teams need review-effort policy, automation-trigger ownership, and auditable routing for when API-triggered reviews run and which effort level they use.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Review workflows should document where API-triggered AI review is allowed, how effort levels are selected, and how human reviewers interpret Balanced as a default rather than a release gate.
qualifying_updates.routing_note: Keep product capability background upstream; local wiki can retain the workflow-control and review-gate implications.

qualifying_updates.title: Copilot deprecates selected models across coding experiences
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: GitHub deprecated Gemini 3.5 Flash, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Kimi K2.7 Code, and Claude Opus 4.7 across Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions, and named suggested alternatives.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Model availability changes can silently affect repeatability of agent prompts, coding workflows, and team instructions. Agent operating guides should avoid hard-coding deprecated model names without a maintenance process.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Team runbooks should treat model names as configurable dependencies with owner review, replacement guidance, and stale-instruction checks.
qualifying_updates.routing_note: Do not create local model-family leaves; retain only the practice note about dependency drift in agent instructions.

qualifying_updates.title: Sonar describes layered review for AI-generated code
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: Sonar described a billing-squad workflow in which generated code is checked by repository instructions, tests, linting, SonarQube analysis, Gitar product-fit review, and then human review. The article states that review time grew as generation got cheaper and that design review remains a weak spot for agents.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The source gives a concrete practice pattern: the agent that writes code should not be the only reviewer, repository instructions should require verification steps, and scope should be calibrated by blast radius.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Potential local lens: layered AI code review where deterministic analysis, product-fit review, and human ownership are separate gates, with instructions that prevent agents from self-signing or committing without human inspection.
qualifying_updates.routing_note: Product and tool descriptions belong upstream; local wiki can capture the review-layer pattern and instruction-file implications.

qualifying_updates.title: AI coding workflow article frames lifecycle controls
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: The article argues that useful AI coding work should define outcomes and acceptance criteria, supply relevant context, plan, set boundaries, build in reviewable increments, verify independently, and keep human review before consequential changes or deployment.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This is a practice-level framing for planning loops, permission boundaries, independent checks, and human approval points. It maps cleanly to local workflow and governance pages without needing broad product coverage.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate synthesis: autonomy should be selected per task by risk, reversibility, permission level, verification strength, and visibility of actions.
qualifying_updates.routing_note: Do not duplicate broad AI workflow taxonomy upstream; preserve only the lifecycle-control implications for local practice.

qualifying_updates.title: AI-coding expectations shift toward specification and accountability
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: The article says developer work shifts from line-by-line implementation toward executable specification, trustworthy context, evaluation of proposals, architecture, security, deployment accountability, and measurement of outcomes rather than generated lines of code.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The update reinforces local adoption guidance: agentic teams need role expectations for context curation, acceptance evidence, security review, and outcome metrics.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Potential local synthesis: measure review time, escaped defects, rework, security findings, and customer impact when assessing AI-assisted development, not only perceived productivity or code volume.
qualifying_updates.routing_note: Survey and platform background belongs upstream; local wiki can retain the operating-model and measurement implications.

qualifying_updates.title: Developer briefing highlights agent package-install and memory risks
qualifying_updates.visible_date: October 2, 2026 in title; page body showed relative age during collection
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: The briefing summarized agent package-install command-injection risk in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Copilot Memory reuse for agentic security autofix, and self-hosted agent deployment. The cited underlying stories include older September sources, so this item is retained as a same-window public practice briefing rather than as primary release evidence.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The practice implication is local and current: package names and dependency manifests are untrusted input to agent tools, execution roles need least privilege, agent memory requires citation validation, and teams need explicit policies for when learned security patterns can influence review.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate governance note: allowlisted package installation is still a privileged agent tool and should be governed like shell access when credentials or execution roles are reachable.
qualifying_updates.routing_note: Treat as a routing note for governance and source-workflow ingest; use primary sources before durable page synthesis.
